newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee down after U.S. stocks news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee down after U.S. stocks news.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures drifted down in subdued trading on anticipated bearish sentiment in New York after the announcement of higher U.S. stocks.
There was origin and trade selling to help the market down, traders said.
Active May closed the morning session $15 lower at $1,297 on volume of 1,091 lots. Total volume was 2,572 lots. It was inflated by crosses, traders said
The market was largely ignoring reports of lower Indonesian production.
"London's just doing its own thing," one trader said. But another felt that U.S. stocks were having some impact.

An increase in U.S. consumer stocks was announced after the close of the market on Wednesday. There was sentiment that they could have an impact in New York and so the numbers were indirectly weighing on London, he said.
Similarly a strike by Colombian dock workers would not affect robustas directly, but it could have an impact on London via New York, traders said.

Indonesia's coffee production is expected to be 10 or 15 per cent below the projected 480,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 (Oct/Sep) coffee year due to bad weather, the chairman of the Association of Indonesian coffee exporters, Oesman Soedargo, said on Thursday.
He also said Indonesia was open to discussion on a move to get members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to cut exports by 2.5 million 60 kg bags in the first half of 1997.
